title: Why the people chose Rama
hook: the second book opens with an old king asking a hall full of people: why Rama?
carry: Rama is dharma in human form

segments.voice: Yesterday, Parashurama's challenge answered: Rama strung the bow, one arrow spent the sage's heavens, and the first book closed at home. Your line was punya: merit is real, and it runs out.

Many people know how the second book of the Ramayana ends: a prince in clothes made of bark, walking into the forest with his wife and his brother. So notice how the Ayodhya Kanda begins. Not with a villain. Not with a quarrel. With an old man who loves his son, and a room full of people who love him too. For the next few weeks, almost everything turns on one family's household, and the first thing in it is good news.
screen: `BARK CLOTHES AND A FOREST: THE END.` → `THE BEGINNING: GOOD NEWS.` → `ONE FAMILY'S HOUSEHOLD.`

segments.voice: Dasharatha has ruled a long time, and he feels it. Rama is the one the whole city talks about. Valmiki pauses to describe him, and one detail stands out. If someone does Rama a single kindness, he is pleased by it. If someone does him a hundred wrongs, he doesn't keep count. So the king makes a plan. He'll name Rama the yuvaraja, the young king, the heir who shares the rule while his father is still alive. He doesn't simply announce it. He calls an assembly: counselors, leading citizens, kings from the lands around, though in his hurry, the text notes, he doesn't send for Janaka or for Bharata's grandfather in Kekaya. If you agree, tell me. If there's a better course, tell me that too. The hall answers with one roar of yes. And the old king tests them: why Rama, while I'm still ruling well? So they tell him. His truthfulness, his courage, his kindness to ordinary people, how he asks after their families and their fields. Here's why this matters to Hindus. Rama is God come down, but the Ramayana keeps showing him as a person you could actually follow. Later in the epic, even an enemy, the demon Maricha, says it plainly: Rama is dharma with a body. That's why grandparents still hold him up to children, and call him maryada purushottam, the best of persons, who keeps within dharma's bounds. Perfect in how he lived it: truthful, kind, a hundred wrongs not counted. And that's why what happens next will hurt so much.
screen: `ONE KINDNESS KEPT, A HUNDRED WRONGS NOT.` · `THE KING ASKS THE ASSEMBLY.` · `WHY RAMA? THE PEOPLE ANSWER.` · `RAMA IS DHARMA WITH A BODY.` · then, large: `MARYADA PURUSHOTTAM.`

segments.voice: Rama kept one kindness and let a hundred wrongs go uncounted. Bring to mind one kindness someone did for you this year, and let it be vivid: the place, the face. If you pray, offer a quiet thank-you for that person, by name. If a hurt from the same person crowds in, let it sit further back for now, and spend the rest of the sit with the kindness.
Yuvaraja, the young king who shares the rule while his father still reigns. Dasharatha proposes Rama for the title, and asks his assembly, which answers with joy.
Your line: Rama is dharma in human form. One kindness kept, a hundred wrongs let go. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 514 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WHY FAST THE NIGHT BEFORE?`

howItsDone: Many Hindu families read the Ayodhya Kanda as the heart of the Ramayana. Rama is often called maryada purushottam, the best of persons who keeps within the bounds of dharma, and his habit of remembering kindness and forgetting wrongs is often held up as a model for children.

original.note: Sanskrit yuvarāja: young king. the heir named while the father still reigns, the title Dasharatha means to give Rama.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama is about to become king.
what it means: he's to be made yuvaraja, heir and co-ruler, while his father still reigns.
what a scholar hears: Valmiki notes that Janaka and the king of Kekaya weren't sent for, a small detail that later readers have taken as a hint of the king's haste.

chat.meaning: Valmiki introduces Rama as the one who keeps one kindness and doesn't count a hundred wrongs, and the people choose him for his truth and kindness. Even an enemy later calls him dharma with a body.

tie.story: Asked why Rama, Ayodhya's assembly listed his truthfulness, courage and kindness, and Valmiki says he kept one kindness and forgot a hundred wrongs.
tie.friend: Priya can tell Sam that's the point: Hindus see in Rama what dharma looks like when a person actually lives it.
